Wearable medical devices are electronic instruments worn on the body to track, record, and transmit real-time physiological data. They bridge everyday wellness and clinical care by offering continuous health monitoring instead of periodic office checkups. [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9330198/)

- **Continuous glucose monitors (CGMs):** Track real-time blood sugar levels for diabetes management via a small sensor.

- **ECG monitors & smartwatches:** Record heart electrical activity to spot irregular rhythms like atrial fibrillation.

- **Wearable blood pressure monitors:** Measure blood pressure patterns outside clinical settings

- **Smart patches & biosensors:** Adhere to the skin to monitor vitals, temperature, or deliver targeted treatments. [](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9330198/)

### Key Benefits

- **Continuous tracking:** Captures data 24/7 rather than a single snapshot during a clinic visit.

- **Early detection:** Alerts patients and doctors to sudden anomalies before emergencies happen.

- **Personalized care:** Supplies doctors with objective historical data to customize treatment plans. [](https://builtin.com/articles/wearable-technology-in-healthcare)

Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGMs):
Devices like subcutaneous sensors track interstitial glucose levels in real time and transmit data to receivers or smartphones.

Smartwatches & Wearable ECG:
Advanced wristwear uses PPG and electrical sensors to log heart rate, blood oxygen, and single-lead ECG rhythms to flag irregularities like atrial fibrillation.
